newsitem.title: UK: London cabbies announce April market float.
newsitem.headline: London cabbies announce April market float.

text.p: London taxi operator Computer Cab Plc said on Tuesday it planned to float its shares on the London Stock Exchange's junior market on April 4, despite opposition from some of its 2,100 drivers,
The Alternative Investment Market float, at 80 pence a share, is expected to raise 3.3 million pounds ($5.3 million) for Computer Cab and value the company at 8.25 million.
It drew protests from some of the capital's traditionally outspoken "cabbies" but was backed by more than 60 percent of members voting last November.
The opposition to the float was centred on questions about the financing of the company's plans for its satellite-based Mobistar cab location and dispatch system.

A minority was against the float, saying they would be contributing to the capital costs of the system, which is based on Global Satellite Positioning (GSP) technology, without receiving any equity in the company.
But now, in spite of continued opposition including a series of legal actions launched by drivers, the float is set to go ahead.
Computer Cab said it intended to consider opportunities for expansion outside of London, both in the UK and abroad. ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
